entry_state: Simulation separates permitted actions, economic events, accounting treatment and atomic state transitions. Conditional report laws remain a family unless a justified measure over histories is supplied; mixture, variance and weight-set bounds have distinct assumptions. Grouping requires equal requested conditional laws, and sampled extrema remain inner exploration. One local notation defect is confirmed: theta in the simulation equations is never defined.
exit_state: Rounded debt can be represented by fixed and floating principal amounts within the rational-linear fragment, with attained and unattained endpoints distinguished. Explicit templates generate a scoped joint family; admissible grouping must preserve transitions and requested reports. The finite probability algorithm has introduced disjoint hypotheses and single-use likelihoods; its failure-mass interpretation continues on the next page.
findings: The rounded-debt reformulation replaces alpha times unknown total debt with principal amounts F and V, explicitly retaining its domain of validity and the zero-principal boundary.
The future-interest infimum 4.975 is attained, while supremum 7.035 is not. Solver timeout, unsupported theory and unboundedness remain distinct from infeasibility.
Template construction retains finite structural cells and continuous formulas, with scoped completeness criteria rather than a claim to enumerate all real histories.
Grouping requires additive transitions and reporting under compatible terms; changed horizons or rules invalidate previous sufficiency. No new defect on pages 90–91.
